question: A team manager wants to change how his team uses Claude, in a way the team's current written standard does not allow. In which order should these steps be taken?
options: A) Write down the proposed change and the data it would involve; update the written standard to match the decision; brief the team on the updated standard; get the policy owner's decision on it.
B) Update the written standard to match the decision; write down the proposed change and the data it would involve; get the policy owner's decision on it; brief the team on the updated standard.
C) Write down the proposed change and the data it would involve; get the policy owner's decision on it; update the written standard to match the decision; brief the team on the updated standard.
D) Brief the team on the current standard; write down the proposed change and the data it would involve; get the policy owner's decision on it; update the written standard to match the decision.
correct_answers: C) Write down the proposed change and the data it would involve; get the policy owner's decision on it; update the written standard to match the decision; brief the team on the updated standard.
explanations: The standard is updated and the team briefed on the updated standard on the strength of an unapproved proposal, with the policy owner asked only at the end, once the change is already in effect.
The standard is amended to match a decision that has not been made yet. Rewriting governance ahead of approval is exactly the shortcut a policy exists to stop.

Correct. A written proposal naming the change and the data involved is what the policy owner needs in order to decide; the decision is what authorises the change; the written standard is then updated to match it; and the team is briefed on the updated standard, which is the one they will actually follow.

The team is briefed on the current standard before anything has changed, so the briefing is out of date as soon as the standard is rewritten, and the update only lands after they have already been informed.
